description: Concrete gravity dam monolith resists hydrostatic water pressure and impounds the elevated reservoir pool.
Submerged reservoir water approaches the upstream intake bar screen under hydrostatic head.
Excess floodwater above full supply level bypasses generation through the gated dam spillway.
Spillway chute and stilling basin dissipate flood energy safely into the downstream river.
Filtered water passes smoothly across the bar screen into the flared concrete intake bellmouth.
Accelerated bellmouth inflow passes through the emergency guard gate shaft.
Open intake gate admits pressurized water into the headrace approach conduit.
Headrace delivers closed-conduit water into the underground rock/concrete-lined pressure tunnel.
Vertical riser tee exchanges transient mass oscillations to cushion pressure waves during gate changes.
Pressurized flow leaves the tunnel beneath the surge tank and enters the steep steel penstock.
High-pressure water descending the penstock arrives at the powerhouse turbine main inlet valve.
Open inlet valve admits pressurized water tangentially into the tapering volute scroll case.
360-degree volute distributes uniform swirling flow radially inward across fixed stay vanes.
Pre-aligned flow enters the pivoting wicket gate cascade for discharge and swirl regulation.
Pivoting wicket gates inject swirl and regulated discharge across the radial vaneless gap into the Francis runner.
15 double-curved blades transfer integrated hydrodynamic pressure and momentum torque into the runner crown and band.
Low-pressure water exits the runner eye axially downward into the expanding draft tube diffuser.
Bolted runner crown transmits shaft torque and axial thrust vertically upward along the forged main shaft.
Hydrodynamic tilting-pad thrust and guide bearings carry vertical rotating mass and constrain radial runout.
Main shaft delivers mechanical rotational power directly into the 24-pole salient-pole generator rotor.
Static thyristor AVR supplies regulated DC excitation current to the rotating rotor field coils.
24 copper pole coils are mounted concentrically on the salient pole bodies of the rotor rim.
Rotating 24-pole magnetic flux sweeps across the air gap to induce three-phase AC EMF in stator coils.
Laminated silicon-steel stator core anchors armature coils and channels magnetic return flux.
Sealed generator barrel encloses the stator, rotor, and closed-loop ventilation air circuit.
Air-to-water finned radiator banks extract core and copper I2R heat from recirculated generator air.
Three-phase stator phase leads terminate at insulated bushings inside the generator terminal box.
Medium-voltage high-current AC enters the three isolated-phase aluminum bus ducts.
Busbar conducts generated power into the three-pole generator synchronizing circuit breaker.
Closed synchronizing breaker feeds 11 kV power into the primary delta windings of the step-up transformer.
High-voltage bushings deliver stepped-up 132 kV AC into the outdoor switchyard protection bay.
Dead-end gantry feeds HV AC onto overhead ACSR conductors suspended on steel lattice towers.
Overhead transmission corridor delivers electrical energy into the synchronized regional power grid.
Expanding concrete elbow discharges decelerated water through twin submerged outlet bays.
Submerged outlet keeps water seal intact while releasing flow smoothly into the tailrace pool.
Wide tailrace channel returns 100% of turbined river volume cleanly into the natural downstream channel.
